sentences.text: The skull of Lacusovagus was long and unusually wide, featuring unusual toothless jaws and lacking a bony head crest.
The genus is based on specimen SMNK PAL 4325, a partial upper jaw containing skull sections in front of the eyes.

The type species L. magnificens means "grand lake wanderer" and refers to its large size, making it the largest pterosaur from the Crato Formation with an estimated 4-meter wingspan and 30 kg body mass.
Lacusovagus was described in 2008 by Mark Witton.
Lacusovagus is classified in the family Chaoyangopteridae, though this placement is sometimes questioned.
The fossil was found in the Nova Olinda Member of the Crato Formation, dating to the Early Cretaceous (probably Aptian stage, 120 to 93 million years ago).
Lacusovagus lived during the Aptian stage, between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
Alternative phylogenetic analyses have placed Lacusovagus within the genus Tupuxuara (family Thalassodromidae) or within Tapejaridae.
